group: layered counter with (110) prefix (rule not found)
title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0LC---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1LC0RE_1LD1LC_1RA0LB_0RD0RF_0LC---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open; the round rule is not found. The machine runs a layered counter: a growing prefix (110)^k is turned, at each reset, into runs of groups of sizes 4, 7, 10, 13, … with large multiplicities, which the following sweeps use up. Nothing beyond the generated bounded runs is proved.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 39,716 cells have been visited and 22,109 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.5). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.1).

claims.title: Prefix, groups and resets
claims.text: At each visit of the left end in state B the tape is B> 00 (110)^k (10)^a₁ 1 (10)^a₂ 1 …. Between resets k grows by 2 a visit and the sweeps merge the groups into runs of sizes 4, 7, 10, 13, …; at a reset the prefix becomes about k/2 groups of size 4. Large and small resets alternate (k = 909, 37, 1670, 220, 2591, 397, 3185 between steps 3.6·107 and 5.3·108). Observed in simulation, not proved.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The carry rule between the levels is the missing piece.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LA1LC_0LC0LF_0RB--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. The machine builds a long run of the word 110 at the left end, then turns it into groups of sizes 4, 7, 10, 13, … that later sweeps use up: a counter with several levels. How the levels carry into each other has not been worked out.

facts.text: Steps simulated from blank tape without a halt.
Group sizes after the sweeps, in long runs.
How the levels interact is not yet known.

sections.heading: A prefix and a list of groups
html: Each time the head reaches the left end in state B, the tape reads

a prefix of k words 110, then a list of groups. Between resets the prefix grows by two words a visit, and the sweeps merge groups so that the list becomes long runs of equal sizes 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, …; at step 2.8·108 it starts
(4^140: 140 groups of size 4 in a row).

sections.heading: The prefix becomes groups
html: When the list is used up far enough, the prefix is turned into about k/2 groups of size 4 and a new round starts. Large and small resets alternate:
The multiplicities of the sizes 4, 7, 10, 13, … act like the digits of a counter with several levels; the rule by which they carry is not worked out.

sections.heading: Not known
html: The machine stops only if the head in state F reads a 1; in 109 simulated steps it never does. Without the carry rule there is no honest estimate either way.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.5). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.1).
After 109 steps the tape spans 39,716 cells (26,775 left of the start, 467 right), with a density of 1s of 0.557.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A layered counter: a growing (110)^k prefix is turned at each reset into runs of groups of sizes 4, 7, 10, 13, …, which the sweeps use up; rule not found; no halt in 10<sup>9</sup> steps.
